posts.title: Forum for posting comments on week 11-12 readings (due Nov 30)

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
ReGroup: Interactive Machine Learning for On-Demand Group Creation in Social Networks

This paper introduce an novel on-demand group creating suggesting system called ReGroup. It uses on-demand user-interface interaction with machine learning to provide a ordered list of friends suggested to be added to the group. The result is that ReGroup is more appreciated for larger and more varied groups. 

This research reminds me of a recently released feature of Facebook, which let you to create a private group with certain friends whenever you share a post. It’s all manually selected with a list of suggesting friends and a search bar. Unlike ReGroup, the suggesting list won’t change along the process, but I think they may be doing the similar research of group creation too. 

A research question arises from this study is interesting to me. How we can come up with the features regardless of profile information or explicit labeled ones, can defined features by observing some other patterns that can lead to less missing data? That is what I want do research.

items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
Crowdfunding Support Tools : Predicting Success and Failure


I find that this paper is very interesting as this tool might be very useful for the one who are doing the crowdfunding. For the one who are in crowdfunding, failure and success is very important as they can predict what should be in consideration of going to further step. I believe if the system has gone live and able to accurately predict the outcome of the crowdfunding, the funding-seeker will be more confident to present a high-quality project that will result a success. Also, from the platform point of view, they can be benefited to show only the high-quality project and it will increase the quality of the platform as well.

In addition, maybe other than using the machine learning technology to predict the success and failure, the funding-seeker can be informed about the reason of such prediction to happen. Then, the funding-seekers are able to hire another people from another domain that eligible to give some advises to the reasons. Then, the funding-seeker will then be able to keep improving and doing iterative work to enhance their project and transform them into a successful project.

items.name: 林奕汝
items.note:
Crowdfunding Support Tools : Predicting Success and Failure

This EA is apparently someone's final project. They took online data with traditional machine learning classification modules, the most usual examples in ML courses, to predict success or failure. This lab even have another two similar EA with HCI perspectives for the same conference, CHI 2013. There's a common question "What's the contribution of this research had for the HCI community?"

items.name: 林奕汝
items.note:
Classifying Driver Workload Using Physiological and Driving Performance Data: Two Field Studies

This research classified the workload of drivers from their heart rate, skin conductance level, speed, and steering wheel position. They define "cognitive load" from on-road data acquisition phase of few different mental load situations, n-back cognitive demand task. Trained with those data, they select effective features and build a classifier as their best.

However, there's a writing mistake. They said, "We have shown that machine learning techniques can be applied to vehicle sensor data as well as driver physiological sensor data to provide recognition of elevated cognitive load periods." In fact, machine learning can be applied to any data with a concrete target. It is better to pronounce "We have shown that machine learning techniques can perform well on vehicle sensor data as well as driver physiological sensor data to provide recognition of elevated cognitive load periods."

The authors proposed a new usable detection for evaluating workload of drivers. For future work, the biggest contribution in this paper might be the final module they tuned. But where is it? It seems to be a developing part of their product (http://agelab.mit.edu/awarecar). Please follow the directions in this paper and build yourselves. It would be great if they can make data and results open to this world as scientists.

items.name: 林奕汝
items.note:
ReGroup: Interactive Machine Learning for On-Demand Group Creation in Social Networks

Amershi et. al (2012) presented a recommending system for members to add into a group. Authors had a survey for features to use and an evaluation after the system had been built. Even though Google and Facebook had similar services, this paper shows a complete research for combining ML and HCI.

items.name: 林奕汝
items.note:
Analyzing Collaborative Learning Processes Automatically: Exploiting the Advances of Computational Linguistics in Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning

The authors presented a framework to analyze four process dimensions of knowledge construction in Computer-supported collaborative learning: (1) participation, (2) epistemic, (3) argument, and (4) social modes of co-construction. As a journal format, this paper includes more details on background and related work. They use four of seven Weinberger and Fischer’s dimensions (2006) as a coding scheme. This paper shown exactly the methods of combining ML with human coders to label out tags in contextual data. They also have a complete evaluation for kappa. It’s a methodological revolution. We can save our vitality and time, maybe, to explore how human think and act.

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
Crowdfunding support tools-predicting success & failure

Recently, research in crowdfunding has recently gained attention in the HCI and CSCW communities. To support novice crowdfunders, the study used machine learning classifiers to predict the chances of successfully funding a Kickstarter project. Their classifier can predict whether a project will be successful with roughly 68% accuracy. However, the current crowdfunding support tool may not provide novices with any assistance. It is more important for novices to know how to improve their projects rather than rates of success.

Machine learning algorithms are being used in lots of places in interesting ways. Yet, a limitation of this study is that the crowdfunding support tool only relies on machine learning to predict the success of a crowdfunding project, so the researchers consider the possibility of using Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to evaluate. After all, machine learning models need training data to work well, and crowdsourcing is the perfect way to get that data. Using crowdsourcing in machine learning helps in combining human insights with machine learning techniques and facilitates better analytical use of unstructured data.

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
Classifying Driver Workload Using Physiological and Driving Performance Data: Two Field Studies

This study applied ML to vehicle sensor data and driver physiological sensor data to explored the role of cognitive workload levels on the driver. The main aim of this study is to improve methods for evaluating automotive user interfaces. Before I read this paper, I only knew that one approach to evaluate user interfaces is usability testing. So, the method the study proposed is novel for me. Additionally, there are two parts of this study we can learn: 1) the large sample size; 2) to stress the contribution to HCI and the benefit that others can gain from the contribution.

items.name: 王玉美
items.note:
ReGroup: Interactive Machine Learning for On-Demand Group Creation in Social Networks 

This paper is really interesting as it tried to combine the machine learning and HCI aspects together. Regarding the system built in the paper, I feel that the idea of using Machine learning to make the group formation recommender is such a brilliant idea. However, if I would need to choose which interface described in the paper, I will still prefer the first interface which is the alphabetical search. Because, when I am making a group, I actually prefer to organize them by myself and it helps me easier to remember who those people in which group. However, if the system is just to help me to categories, the people in friend list I have, then the second interface might be very helpful. There, I agree with the statement by the author that mention that different interface will be useful in different circumstances. Hence, when we are designing something, we should be really careful of putting the scope of our interface and it is okay not to cater for all conditions and circumstances.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
ReGroup: Interactive Machine Learning for On-Demand Group Creation in Social Networks

This work presents ReGroup to help people organize custom groups, which learns a person's interaction of adding members to a group. ReGroup uses a Naive Bayes classifier to find similarities between users and then make recommendations. Their evaluation shows that the traditional search-by-name approach is suitable for small and well-defined groups where members are easy to recall by name while ReGroup is efficient for larger and more varied groups. However, I think there is a need for comparison what option is easier and faster for the users.

items.name: 李柏翰
items.note:
Crowdfunding Support Tools: Predicting Success & Failure

Michael et al.(2013) studied the initial attributes (e.g. goal, rewards, external links...) of a kickstart product and predict whether one will success or not. The motivation is quite encouraging since the automatic mechanism resulting from the study could play a helpful role for guiding creative individuals to better showcase their product. In the finding, however, authors did not show the key attributes among 12 attributes, which I think should have been an important part to share in the finding section.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
Crowdfunding support tools - predicting success and failure

Upon considering the attributes used to classify the potential success of projects upon launch, it may be useful to consider how trends between these attributes may not necessarily be as predictive of success as they may seem. For example, reward_count, or the number of rewards available, is one of the attributes fed into the classifier to make trait comparisons. However, the number of rewards available to an investor may not be as relevant as the nature of the rewards. Such information as this may still be able to be utilized in the classifier if qualitative evaluation is done on the corpus of data from kickstarter to identify possible key categories or types of rewards, and these categories may be used to calculate how reward type factors into the results of the decision tree algorithm. The idea is that to identify more relevant attributes for a crowdfunder to use, it may be useful to do deeper processing on the data to dig out more pertinent information before running the classifier.

items.name: 劉  淨
items.note:
Crowdfunding Support Tools: Predicting Success & Failure

The goal of this work is to develop tools to enable novice creators reach their fundraising goal on crowdfunding platform. They train machine learning classifiers to determine whether projects will be successful before they launch. They use a pre-scraped dataset from Kickstarter. The attributes(features) are pre-decided according to the structure of project on Kickstarter. They evaluated the performance of classifiers between various decision tree algorithms and support vector machines with different kernel functions. There result shows that their model can predict the success of a crowdfunding project with 68% accuracy. 

My main concern on this work is they way the identify attributes seems to depend on platform instead of the content of a project. Without rigorous justifying how they decide the attributes make me feel concern on generalizability of their model.

items.name: 楊馥名
items.note:
ReGroup: Interactive Machine Learning for On-Demand Group Creation in Social Networks

As mentioned in the paper, ReGroup is a very suitable and effective application of machine learning to this specific problem, as creating large and varied groups on-demand is a more difficult task for a person who has to effectively consider the characteristics of a very large number of individuals. The interactive element of this model effectively takes a step forward from the mentioned existing implementations of related auto-group creators that just create and then have the user manually edit the machine-inferred result by taking notice that the user's manual edits is also useful information for the system to continually integrate in an iterative manner.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
Crowdfunding Support Tools: Predicting Success & Failure

This work proposes a tool to provide an indicator to a novice creators for determining if the project is likely to succeed. They use a pre-scraped dataset of a project page from kickstarter and then evaluate the performance of various machine learning methods, including SVM and decision trees. The results show that the decision trees provide the highest accuracy and run the fastest. However, I think there is a problem of generalizing their model to the real world because they only consider the attributes they listed. I think they should include more features for prediction, such as the content of projects and current affairs.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
ReGroup: Interactive Machine Learning for On-Demand Group Creation in Social Networks

In my view, the most meaningful finding about this research is "different techniques are effective for different types of groups". I have never think about the potential problems about grouping and always used to do it through Facebook. It is perhaps because we usually just care about the small groups like teams for school course, larger one we want to group actively is just the classmates group. Although the original intention of ReGroup is not for different groups, this finding still made me realize that we could more pay attention to the things, people around us for doing the HCI research.

items.name: 鍾祐霖
items.note:
Classifying Driver Workload Using Physiological and Driving Performance Data: Two Field Studies

This paper gives a very detailed experiment designing and conducting process. From identifying which features to measure and why these features are chosen, to recruiting participants, practicing the procedures, and analyzing the results. I learned a lot both from the overall structure of the paper and the usage of machine learning in the study. Since I’m taking machine learning course right now, it is really important to know where can we actually take the model in practice to benefit the real world, and this paper gives me an interesting and not cliche situation that machine learning can help.

items.name: 蔡守恩
items.note:
Crowdfunding Support Tools:Predicting Success & Failure  

This work focused on prediction of whether one crowdfunding project can be successful. It provides the novice creator to indicate their project before posting on the crowdfunding website. I think i just a prediction of the beginning status so that its correct rate is unable to be higher to 80~90%. Since that whole crowdfunding process is fluctuated, people don't just judge whether they want to donate by the one single moment. But I think maybe it's just initial research and would go deeper, so I want to know how the team choose and analyze the in-crowdfunding process, is using NLP to tackle the comments, is calculating viral effect on social network or maybe some variables that doesn't occur to me.

items.name: 張儷齡
items.note:
Classifying Driver Workload Using Physiological and Driving Performance Data: Two Field Studies

I have once consider about the issue about driver when i was learning car driving.It was about people feeling about the waiting time and color of traffic lights and also the appearance of zone out.Then i found there was lots of similar topic and some worthwhile result that had changed our traffic light regulations.But this paper combined the machine learning and  driver’s cognitive load together and showed an automatic  cognitive workload classifier that could classify cognitive load across individuals with high accuracy. We don't need to build a custom model. The application of machine learning made the issue of driver’s cognitive load became an interesting issue.

items.name: 李若彤
items.note:
ReGroup: Interactive Machine Learning for On-Demand Group Creation in Social Networks

The study developed a machine learning system called ReGroup that helps users to create custom groups in social networks. The opinions of the participants and the results showed that each option creation techniques are better depending on the size of the group. Alphabetical order is better for small groups, and ReGroup is better for large groups.

In my experience, I did feel frustrated, when selecting people from a large friend list before creating an online group. The study is considerately related to our life. It also presented an interesting research that combines HCI and machine learning to apply in social networks.

items.name: 李柏翰
items.note:
ReGroup : Interactive Machine Learning for On-Demand Group Creation in Social Networks

This paper presented ReGroup, a machine learning model specialized for helping recommending new users to a specific group. By modeling 18 features, it itself re-learn iteratively when people add new users into such group, however the size(of the group) matters a lot, which resulted in different accuracy between models.

To compare with the recommendation system like (Netflix), which use the past movie to recommend new movie for users, I think recommending people in a social network is more complicated and more active during the process.

items.name: 姚舜懷
items.note:
Classifying Driver Workload Using Physiological and Driving Performance Data: Two Field Studies

The paper applies machine learning to classify evaluated cognitive load and explore the differences between training classifiers within individuals and across individuals, such as decision tree, logistic regression, and Naive Bayes. Through 10-fold cross validation it shows that classifiers can achieve reasonable accuracy by simple features and classification algorithms. I do learn a lot about experiment design and the procedure of applying machine learning from this paper. It gives me a good example about HCI and machine learning research.
